lesson.child_mission: Adding integers models signed changes: +a moves right a units; −a moves left a units. Same signs: add magnitudes and keep the sign. Opposite signs: subtract magnitudes and take the sign of the larger magnitude.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Compute (−6) + 2 and 5 + (−9) with a number-line or sign rule explanation for each.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: −4 and −4; explanations mention direction or magnitude rules correctly.

WATCH FOR
Always attaching the first number’s sign blindly after subtracting magnitudes.

INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Solve twelve mixed integer additions, show number-line or rule notes for four of them, and self-check with a reverse jump.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Start at 2; add −5: jump left 5 to −3, so 2 + (−5) = −3. Same-sign: (−4) + (−3) = −7. Opposite: (−4) + 9 = 5.

TRY FIRST
Compute (−6) + 2 and 5 + (−9) with a number-line or sign rule explanation for each.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: −4 and −4; explanations mention direction or magnitude rules correctly.
teach_steps.explain:
Adding integers models signed changes: +a moves right a units; −a moves left a units. Same signs: add magnitudes and keep the sign. Opposite signs: subtract magnitudes and take the sign of the larger magnitude.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
